answer: Producing a novel, coherent answer each epoch is cheap per alias but prohibitive across thousands, so scale buys less credibility — the attacker cannot simply buy a large, credible flock. This is durable because the trusted grader set only grows through bootstrap capacity, preventing a sudden takeover by a large new flock. The upshot is a network where trust is a resource you earn, not a quantity you can mint — and that is what keeps Sybil attacks economically unviable. Consider a trellis as the anchor of the cost. A signal stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a vine holds...
